fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly to distinguish it from any secondary drive or parking area approach.
• Post visible signage or markings at the secondary access point so responders can identify it quickly without prior knowledge of the property.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and unobstructed vehicle passage from the street to the residence.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and move around it without obstruction.
• Clear a defined walking path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for responders carrying equipment.
• Keep the walkway between structures free of stored items, planters, or landscaping that would slow or block foot movement.
• Mark the water feature boundary with a visible indicator so responders moving quickly across the lawn area at night are aware of the hazard.
• Install lighting or reflective markers along the walkway leading to the rear of the property to support nighttime navigation.
• If a gate controls rear access, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-Box or coded lock so responders do not have to force entry.
• Identify and mark the rear access point with a sign or reflective marker so responders can locate it without circling the property.
• Designate and keep clear a flat

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees and the building.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees close to the structure to raise the canopy height off the ground.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep shrubs and low plants near the structure trimmed short and separated from one another.
• Clear dead or dry ground vegetation from beneath tree clusters near the building.
• Maintain open lawn or ground cover areas between tree clusters and the structure by preventing shrub or brush encroachment.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their full length.
